To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the generalization performance and stability of GAN training algorithms are closely linked and (2) the generalization of GANs is improved if the minimization and the maximization problems are solved simultaneously with a learning rate proportional to the ratio of the Lipschitz constants of their respective objective functions.
the stability of the gradient descent ascent algorithm depends on the choice of the learning rates for the minimization and the maximization problems.

the stability properties of the minimax optimization problem depend on the choice of the optimization algorithm and the generalization performance can be improved by using a more stable optimization algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of optimization algorithm in the generalization properties and training stability of the learned model in the minimax learning setup.
the generalization properties, not only the convergence properties, of minimax optimization algorithms.
the stability of gradient based minimix optimization algorithms, their role in the generalizaion performance of the learned minimix models, and their implications for the success and design of GANs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of GANs, the optimization algorithm plays a key role not only in the convergence speed but also in the generalization properties.
the optimization algorithm plays a key role both in the training and the generalization of GANs.
the optimization algorithm plays a crucial role in the generalizability of minimax learners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimization algorithm plays a dual role in minimax optimization, both in convergence and generalization.
the choice of the optimization algorithm can be used as an effective regularization mechanism for improving the generalization of learned models.
a good optimization algorithm is not sufficient to achieve good generalization in minimax problems, and the optimization algorithm must be chosen in conjunction with the learning rate schedule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the optimization algorithm can be as important as the choice of the loss function for the generalization performance in minimax problems.
the choice of the optimization algorithm can be as important as that of the loss function in the design of a minimax learning problem.
, while faster convergence may be a good indicator of the quality of the learned model in terms of training error, it does not necessarily guarantee a good generalization error.
